title: Pivot Points (Camarilla)
summary: Four supports and four resistances placed tightly around the previous period's close, each a fixed fraction of that period's range away from it.
description:
Camarilla pivots build their levels around the previous period's close rather than around a central pivot. Each level is the previous close plus or minus a fixed fraction of the previous period's range: the range times 1.0833, 1.1666, 1.25 and 1.5, each divided by 12, for levels one to four. That puts R1 and S1 about 9 percent of the range from the close and R4 and S4 one eighth of the range from it, so the levels are much tighter than classic pivots.

The study also draws the classic central pivot, the average of the previous high, low and close. The period can be a day, a Monday-start week or a calendar month. The chart's own bars are folded into those periods, and every bar of a period reads the high, low and close of the period before it, so the levels hold steady through each period.
howToRead:
Because the levels sit close to the previous close, price reaches several of them in a normal period. A common reading treats R3 and S3 as the edges of the expected range, where traders look for price to turn back, and R4 and S4 as breakout levels, where a move beyond them suggests the range has given way.

The levels describe the previous period's range and close, nothing more. On a day that opens far from the previous close, most levels can be left behind at once, and the reading of turns and breakouts no longer applies.

faq.q: Why are the levels centred on the close and not on the pivot?
faq.a: That is how this method is defined: every support and resistance is the previous close plus or minus a fraction of the previous range. The central pivot line is drawn as well for reference, but no level is built from it.

faq.q: Do the levels move during the day?
faq.a: No. Every bar of a period reads the period before it, which has already closed, so the lines are fixed for the whole period and step to new values when the next one begins.

faq.q: Why are there no levels at the start of the chart?
faq.a: The levels come from the previous completed period. Until the chart holds one whole day, week or month of bars, there is no completed period to read, so the first period on the chart carries no lines.
